parsedVerdict.reasoning: src/domain/stock-reservation-service.ts passes: it is a domain service, and everything it does is business logic. The all-or-nothing reservation rule ("Reserves every line or none of them") is a business rule. The `canReserve` checks in `reserve()` and the quantity totals in `totalByProduct()` are also business logic. Both throw domain errors (`NotFoundError`, `InsufficientStockError`) when a check fails. The file reads and writes data only through the `ProductRepository` interface, which lives in the domain layer. There is no database code, HTTP code or framework code in the file. It also has no use-case concerns like transactions, DTO mapping or authorization; the application use cases inject this service and handle those. One could argue the `findById`/`save` sequence is application-level orchestration. However, a domain service that works with an abstract repository to enforce a rule spanning several products is a standard domain-layer pattern, so this is not a misplaced responsibility.
